business_problem: Novartis R&D needs to turn large volumes of scientific, clinical, operational, and real-world data into faster, higher-quality decisions across drug discovery and development, reducing cycle times, surfacing safety risks earlier, and improving trial planning in a domain where success rates are low and delays are costly.
solution_summary: Novartis describes an in-house, AI-enabled R&D decision-support approach that spans research, preclinical work, clinical development, and documentation. Data is ingested from human genetic and multi-omic datasets, imaging, clinical trial results, decades of published research, real-world evidence, protein information, prior chemistry, and clinical and operational study data. AI models are used to integrate these sources for target identification and validation, while generative chemistry methods explore molecular design spaces and optimize multiple properties in parallel. In development, Generative AI paired with knowledge graphs summarizes prior studies and evidence to support protocol drafting, and trial computational twins simulate what-if clinical design scenarios. AI-enhanced analytics monitor supply, recruitment, and study risks and recommend next best actions. The article does not name a storage platform, but it does describe approved-source workflows, privacy and quality controls, and expert human review before outputs are used in regulated R&D decisions.

solution_components.name: AI models
solution_components.role: Integrate genetic, multi-omic, imaging, clinical, and literature evidence to identify and validate drug targets.

solution_components.name: Generative AI
solution_components.role: Summarizes prior studies and evidence for trial design and creates structured first drafts of clinical and regulatory documentation.

solution_components.name: knowledge graphs
solution_components.role: Provide structured context alongside Generative AI to summarize what has and has not worked across prior studies and real-world evidence.

solution_components.name: trial computational twins
solution_components.role: Simulate the operational implications of clinical design choices so teams can test what-if scenarios faster.

solution_components.name: AI-enhanced analytics
solution_components.role: Surface early risk signals across supply, monitoring, and recruitment and recommend next best actions to keep studies on track.

data_flow: Novartis feeds genetic, multi-omic, imaging, trial, literature, real-world, protein, chemistry, clinical, and operational data into AI models and analytics. Those models generate target insights, molecule proposals, safety signals, protocol summaries, trial simulations, and study-risk recommendations, which are then reviewed by Novartis scientists and clinicians to guide R&D, trial design, and regulatory documentation.
business_outcome: Novartis aims to reduce drug discovery and development timelines, improve decision quality, surface risks earlier, shorten iterative cycles, and help teams bring therapies to patients faster with a higher likelihood of success.
metrics: less than 10 percent of drug candidates historically reach the market
architecture_clues: The approach is designed to be reused across therapeutic areas, teams, and geographies.
Privacy, safety, and quality controls are embedded throughout the workflow.
Novartis combines internal tool development with external AI collaborations when off-the-shelf tools are insufficient for regulated science.
Documentation outputs are generated from approved sources and then reviewed and refined by Novartis experts.
